item.summary: refactor(gateway): retire the legacy numeric ChatAbortMarker and dead registry surface (#124108) Abort markers are process-local in-memory state (nothing persists them), so the numeric ChatAbortMarker variant — in-process rollout compat for #91013 — has been unreachable in production since every producer moved to createChatAbortMarker. Deleting it also kills the registeredAtMs timestamp fallback in isChatAbortMarkerCurrent, which makes ChatRunEntry.registeredAtMs entirely write-only; the sequence comparison is the sole ordering authority. Dead surface riders (same owner file): - ChatRunRegistry.clear had zero callers (restart teardown clears through chatRunState.clear, which owns the whole store). - createChatRunRegistry/createToolEventRecipientRegistry standalone factories were consumed only by tests; production always goes through createChatRunState. Tests now use the state-owned instances, and the server-chat barrel re-exports are gone. Net -32 production LOC; 462 tests across the five touched suites green.
